findings.problem: status is a public String field. Any string value ("sent", "", "SENT", null-prefixed) is representable. The domain invariant — a frame has exactly one lifecycle phase — is not enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate FrameWorkflow into an inconsistent state (e.g. status="draft" with is_sent=true), making runtime checks fragile and tests unable to cover all illegal combinations.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a sealed enum `pub status: FrameStatus` where `FrameStatus` variants are `Draft`, `Validated`, `Sent`. Remove `is_sent` entirely.

findings.problem: is_validated is a bare bool. A bool can only express two states (true/false) with no domain semantics. It cannot encode the ordering invariant (must be validated before sent).
findings.failure_mode: A frame can be marked validated and then un-validated, or sent without being validated — both illegal. No compiler-enforced transition order exists.
findings.fix: Remove `is_validated: bool`. Encode validated as an intermediate typestate variant or derive it from the `FrameStatus` enum (e.g. `FrameStatus::Validated` implies validated).

findings.problem: is_sent is a bare bool. It duplicates information already in `status: String` and creates the classic two-field inconsistency problem.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent and status can diverge (e.g. is_sent=true, status="draft"). Every consumer must check both fields and risk missing one.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool`. Let `FrameStatus::Sent` alone answer whether the frame was sent. Derive `sent_at_epoch_ms` presence from the typestate.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a mutating function that takes FrameWorkflow by value and mutates it in-place. It has no preconditions (cannot validate transition rules), no typed error return, and performs a heap allocation ("sent".to_string()).
findings.failure_mode: Without a typestate, mark_sent cannot prevent illegal transitions at compile time. The .to_string() allocates on every call even when the status was already "sent". No caller can distinguish a genuine send from a no-op re-send.
findings.fix: Replace with a fallible, typestate-gated function: `fn try_advance_to_sent(frame: FrameWorkflow) -> Result<FrameWorkflow, TransitionError>` that takes a typestate-bound input (e.g. `FrameValidated`) and returns `FrameSent`. Remove string mutation.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() performs an unconditional heap allocation on every call to mark_sent, even when the status is already "sent" or when a string is unnecessary.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every call path degrades latency and defeats zero-cost abstraction promises. In a hot path (e.g. message processing), this adds GC pressure and tail-latency spikes.
findings.fix: Replace the String status with an enum (zero-cost, no allocation). If string representation is needed for display, implement Display on the enum and format only at the I/O boundary.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain constraints. No newtype wraps it to enforce format rules (length, allowed characters) at construction time.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can pass an empty, oversized, or malformed id into the core. Validation is scattered instead of enforced at the boundary.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct FrameId(String)` (or `NonEmptyString`) with a fallible constructor that validates format. Use `FrameId` in `FrameWorkflow`.

findings.problem: All fields of FrameWorkflow are public and directly mutable. No encapsulation, no invariant enforcement point.
findings.failure_mode: Any module in the crate can mutate any field without going through a typed transition, breaking invariants.
findings.fix: Make fields private and expose access via methods or builder pattern. Or better: make FrameWorkflow an opaque type where construction only happens via fallible constructors.

findings.problem: The crate has zero tests. No behavior contract exists for mark_sent or FrameWorkflow lifecycle.
findings.failure_mode: No regression protection. Any future change to the type or function is untested by definition.
findings.fix: Add behavior tests covering: valid transition (draft→sent), rejected invalid transition (sent→sent), and typestate construction.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or FrameWorkflow. No allocation or latency evidence is available.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that the zero-cost claim holds. The .to_string() allocation on the hot path is unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or divan benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocations (Allocation::Bytes) and latency across warm/cold paths.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or FrameWorkflow operations
no profiler data (flamegraph/crates-flame) for allocation hot paths
no allocation audit (e.g. alloc_counter or miri leak check)
no second-ring evidence (no assembly or dropshot for bounds-check removal claims)
no command evidence (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test not run)
no behavior test suite exists for lifecycle transitions
residual_risk: The crate is a typestate anti-pattern: three independent boolean/string fields encode a lifecycle that should be a single enum or typestate. No tests, no benchmarks, no error taxonomy. Every field is public and mutable. This is a BLOCKER for delivery — the entire struct must be restructured with an enum typestate before any further work. Without typestate, no amount of clippy linting or micro-optimization can prevent illegal states.
